description:
About the Position

Lund University invites applications for a doctoral student in medical science with a orientation toward health sciences (halsovetenskap), within the PRO-COG project. The project studies how people with cognitive disabilities experience and navigate public environments, and how society can design environments and services that support participation for this group. The doctoral candidate will use qualitative methods - interviews, observations and co-creative approaches - to build knowledge that can inform health-care practice, urban planning and disability policy.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment under the Swedish collective agreement, based in Lund University's health-sciences research environment. The doctoral candidate will receive training in qualitative research methodology, work closely with participants and user organisations, and contribute to publications and dissemination aimed at both academic and practice audiences. The research programme involves collaboration across disciplines including occupational therapy, public health and social sciences.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in health sciences, public health or a related field, with training or demonstrated experience in qualitative methods. An interest in disability research, participation and accessibility is central, and experience of working with vulnerable groups is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Lund University's Varbi recruitment portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a personal letter describing the applicant's methodological experience and motivation.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD in medical science (health sciences)
  • PRO-COG project on cognitive disabilities
  • Public environments, participation and accessibility
  • Qualitative methods and co-creative approaches
  • Interdisciplinary health-sciences environment at Lund
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Lund University

Lund University, founded in 1666, is one of Sweden's largest and most international universities and a member of the League of European Research Universities. Its faculties cover engineering, science, medicine, economics, humanities, social sciences, law and the performing arts, and the nearby Copenhagen area makes the Oresund region a strong research hub. Doctoral students are salaried employees under Swedish collective agreements, and postdoctoral fellowships are advertised through the university's Varbi recruitment portal. The university ranks among the top 100 research universities worldwide in major rankings.
